description:
LaunchPad is a student-led team passionate about space exploration, AI and healthcare innovation. Our project, Helios focuses on astronaut health monitoring through an intelligent application.

Team:
• Ayden Liju (UAE): Concept, research, project planning and presentation.
• Diya Manoj (UAE): Lead application development and core functionality.
• Dinah Manoj (UAE): Application development, interface and UI/UX design.
summary:
Helios is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and support system designed to improve the physical and mental well-being of astronauts during long-duration space missions. At its core is an intelligent health-monitoring chip that collects and analyses astronaut health data, helping identify potential health concerns and providing personalised recommendations and possible solutions.
Helios also features an AI-powered robotic companion dog, Medibot, which acts as an additional support system. It assists astronauts by providing health-related guidance, encouraging physical activity, supporting mental well-being and helping locate essential supplies. By combining intelligent health monitoring with interactive robotic assistance, Helios aims to make space missions safer, healthier and more sustainable, while reducing the challenges astronauts face when living far from Earth.
details:
Helios is designed as an integrated astronaut healthcare ecosystem that combines intelligent health monitoring, AI-assisted analysis and robotic support.

How it works:

The central component is a health-monitoring chip that collects and displays astronaut health information. An AI-powered system analyses the collected data, identifies potential health concerns and provides personalised recommendations to help astronauts manage their well-being. This allows astronauts to monitor their health and receive guidance while operating in the isolated environment of space.

Medibot – Robotic Companion:

As a supporting feature, Helios includes Medibot, an AI-powered robotic dog that acts as an interactive health assistant. It helps astronauts follow exercise routines, provides daily wellness check-ins, offers companionship, helps locate essential medical supplies and communicates important health alerts.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

Helios aims to improve astronaut safety, support physical and mental well-being and make healthcare more accessible during long-duration space missions. By combining continuous health monitoring with interactive robotic assistance, the system could help astronauts respond to health concerns earlier and reduce their dependence on immediate assistance from Earth.

Innovation and Creativity:

The main innovation is bringing health-monitoring technology and robotic assistance together into one connected ecosystem. Rather than focusing only on detecting health concerns, Helios also focuses on providing astronauts with practical support and guidance.

Development Considerations:

The project considers the challenges of limited medical assistance, isolation, communication delays, restricted resources and the demanding conditions of space environments. Its proposed design focuses on accessibility, reliability, astronaut safety and adaptability for future space exploration.
